title: Human-Centered Design Is an Evidence Practice

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: We have an experience brief, a usability scorecard, and a service map. Is that what makes CarePath human-centered?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Only if they can change a decision. In this lesson, we'll test the team's favorite explanation for why people abandon booking.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: They say the form is too long. I can cut fields.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Maybe. What else could explain the drop-off?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: People might not know which service they need. Their referral might be missing. The available times might not fit work. Or they may be afraid to submit the wrong information.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Good. Which evidence would tell those explanations apart?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: The funnel shows where people leave, not why. I should watch real attempts and ask what people believed was happening.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: And talk with staff. They see what happens after an incomplete referral enters the service.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: When I watch Maya, she keeps moving between the form, her referral message, a calendar, and an insurance document. The fields aren't the only work.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Calls, mismatched referrals, and manual re-entry. The form isn't just long; information is fragmented.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Could a shorter form still help?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Yes, but I shouldn't make it the whole intervention. I'd test clearer evidence requirements, referral status, saved progress, and a staff view that shares the same state.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Write down the decision, the assumption, the evidence, and what would change your mind. What's missing from your evidence so far?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: People who cannot begin online at all. We need offline recruitment, or we'll call the service improved while leaving them out.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: That's the practice: evidence and participation while choices are still changeable, then learning again after release.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: So ‘human-centered’ isn't a workshop label. It's whether what we learn can reshape the work.
